external_entities.name: colleagues
external_entities.description: Colleagues who sign in through the identity broker.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.

external_entities.name: franchise colleagues
external_entities.description: Colleagues from franchise stores who use their own identity provider.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them

external_entities.name: HR system
external_entities.description: The HR system that supplies group membership changes and leaver information.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Group membership is not maintained there by hand — it comes from the HR system overnight.

external_entities.name: identity provider
external_entities.description: The identity provider used by franchise colleagues.
external_entities.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them
external_entities.notes: The text does not name which colleagues this provider is allowed to vouch for.

processes.name: identity broker
processes.description: Signs colleagues in, issues tokens, signs tokens, and supplies the public signing key.
processes.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.
processes.notes: The broker also accepts sign-in assertions from the franchise identity provider.

processes.name: store admin console
processes.description: An application that permits holders of a store-manager token to change prices and void transactions.
processes.source_excerpt: The store admin console is one of those applications.
processes.notes: The console does not check which store the colleague belongs to, so a store-manager token works against every store.

data_stores.name: key store
data_stores.description: A store holding the signing key used by the identity broker.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.
data_stores.notes: The text does not state where the key store runs or whether it is encrypted at rest.

data_stores.name: broker directory
data_stores.description: The identity broker's directory of colleagues and their group memberships.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.
data_stores.notes: The text does not state where the directory runs or whether it is encrypted at rest.

data_stores.name: audit log
data_stores.description: A log to which the broker writes sign-ins.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down what the log records, whether it covers the franchise route, or whether it is encrypted where it sits.

data_flows.name: sign-in
data_flows.description: Colleagues sign in through the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are

data_flows.name: sign-in
data_flows.description: Franchise colleagues sign in through their own identity provider.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them

data_flows.name: vouch for sign-in
data_flows.description: The franchise identity provider vouches for franchise colleagues to the broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in

data_flows.name: use token
data_flows.description: Colleagues use an issued token with the store admin console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every application takes that token and decides what the colleague may do from the groups in it.
data_flows.data_description: token containing staff id and group list

data_flows.name: fetch public key
data_flows.description: The store admin console fetches the public half of the signing key from the broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Applications fetch the public half from the broker to check the signature.

data_flows.name: read signing key
data_flows.description: The identity broker reads the signing key it uses to sign tokens.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_flows.name: update directory
data_flows.description: The identity broker maintains colleague and group membership information in its directory.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.

data_flows.name: pull changes
data_flows.description: The broker pulls group membership and leaver changes from the HR system overnight.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker pulls the changes once a night

data_flows.name: write sign-ins
data_flows.description: The identity broker writes sign-in events to the audit log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network on which the identity broker and store admin console run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The broker runs on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: home devices
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: including their own devices at home

trust_boundaries.name: franchise stores
trust_boundaries.description: The franchise environment whose colleagues use their own identity provider.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: We also let the franchise stores in.

assumptions.assumption: The key store contains confidential data because it holds a signing key.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the key store holds the broker's signing key.

assumptions.assumption: The broker directory contains confidential data because it holds colleagues and their group memberships.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the directory holds colleagues and the groups they are in.

assumptions.assumption: The audit log contains confidential data because it holds sign-in records.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the broker writes sign-ins to the audit log.
